what: How the self-righting maneuvers in sim/righting_maneuvers.json were found (sim/search_righting.py), and what the search showed. Numbers are from the search sessions; the final success rates of the stored maneuvers are in righting.json (sim/test_righting.py).
method: Cross-entropy search over 4-phase open-loop maneuvers (4 arm joint targets, 3 wheel speeds, duration, arm speed per phase; arm acceleration limit 30 rad/s^2). Cost: tilt left after letting go and settling, plus half the smallest tilt reached on the way; candidates whose arm would pass through the chassis are penalised. First pass: 48 random candidates per generation, one scenario each. Second pass (robust refinement): the best first-pass candidate as the starting mean, 45 candidates per generation, each judged on 3 perturbed scenarios (arm calibration 1 deg, roller friction +-20 %, chassis mass +-8 %, resting pose +-3 deg and any heading), the same 3 for every candidate.

first_pass.side_l: 1440 candidates (30 generations): 2 reached upright, and those two succeeded in only 3 of 24 fresh perturbed scenarios (a needle in the parameter space; the population collapsed back to 'no effect' after finding it). 160 further random candidates: 2 upright, 1 ended leaning on the front wheels and the gripper at 61.8 degrees (the 'fwd' pose, from which the 'fwd' maneuver gets up).
first_pass.fwd: 13-24 of 48 candidates upright in every generation (an easy pose); best candidate 23 of 24 fresh perturbed scenarios.
first_pass.back: 1 of 1440 reached upright, 1 of 24 on fresh scenarios. Dropped: once the lidar head and its standoffs are solid in the model, a robot dropped nose-up no longer settles on its back (it ends on its side), so this pose is not in the library.

robust_refinement.side_l: Generation 5 (of 40 planned, stopped there): 3 of 3 training scenarios upright. On 24 fresh scenarios 24/24; with harsher perturbations (arm offset 2 deg, friction +-30 %, mass +-15 %) 23/24 (model without the solid lidar head). With the solid lidar head: 24/24 and 24/24.
robust_refinement.side_r: Mirror image of the side_l maneuver (shoulder pan sign flipped, wheel 0 and 2 swapped with signs flipped, wheel 1 sign flipped): 24/24 fresh scenarios without re-searching.

chain: A maneuver that only gets from the side to the forward-lean pose, followed by the 'fwd' maneuver, got up in 8 of 12 perturbed scenarios without any robustness search on the first stage: the library works as a chain, and the supervisor re-classifies the pose after each attempt (up to 3 attempts).
caveats: All of this is in the simulator. Contact friction, servo acceleration limits, the cables and the battery position of the real robot are not in it.

The maneuvers were searched with the arm in the carry pose. Knock-overs with the arm reaching down in front with the gripper open (what a grasp looks like): 9 of 16 fell, all 9 got up with the same maneuvers (results/righting_arm_out.json). Arm raised, or the gripper holding something: not tried.
Only the lidar head and its standoffs are solid on top of the chassis; the camera mount and other parts are not modelled, so real rest poses may differ.
